faqs.q: How much does a Chinese Crested cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $500–$2,000 for a Chinese Crested puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Budget $120–$200 per month for a Chinese Crested, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Small breeds often cost less on food and some products, but vet bills don't proportionally reduce — procedures cost similar amounts regardless of size.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($300–600), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Chinese Crested cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Chinese Crested are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $1,500–$3,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Chinese Cresteds shed a lot?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Chinese Crested need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Chinese Crested's hairless coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Chinese Cresteds that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds easy to train?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Chinese Cresteds. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Most Chinese Cresteds learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Chinese Cresteds commonly have?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are most commonly associated with dental disease. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Chinese Cresteds live?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds have an average lifespan of 13–18 years. Small breeds often live longer than large breeds. Dental care is particularly important for small dogs, as dental disease is a common longevity issue.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Chinese Cresteds than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Chinese Crested at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Chinese Crested puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Chinese Crested puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Chinese Crested-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds good with kids?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Chinese Cresteds get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Chinese Cresteds bark a lot?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their compact nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Chinese Crested need per day?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds good running partners?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Chinese Crested doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Chinese Crested be off-lead?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: A Chinese Crested needs approximately ½–1½ cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Adult Chinese Cresteds should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Chinese Cresteds do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Chinese Crested from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Small breeds typically transition to adult food around 12 months. Moving too late keeps them on higher-calorie puppy formulas that can cause weight gain in lower-activity adults.

faqs.q: Is a Chinese Crested a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Chinese Cresteds good family dogs?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Chinese Cresteds do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Chinese Cresteds form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Chinese Crested?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Chinese Crested — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
